candidates.label: 011-pr-wire-port-floor-checks
candidates.summary: port of r10-F2-010 into F1 with no change of gates, angles or angle-shift map (parity frame; L: 0 -> ~p_t&~s_r via the (1 3) 7-T Fredkin, converted to g = ~p_t&(p_r^p_l); a = f&~g for the (0 2) Fredkin; Bell decoders (0,1),(2,3); w23 fused onto a, w01 toggled onto the p_r wire inside the H(f) window; 9-term R_x walk in 9 CX between free ends {t, l, g} and {r, t}); round-11 F1 checked the CX, T and depth floors of this datapath and found no strict improvement, so this program records the tie (83, 638, 1521, 10).

candidates.label: 011-h-line-seven-rotations
candidates.summary: T-lean Pareto variant of r10-F2-010 (same leg: parity frame, L: 0 -> ~p_t&~s_r [(1 3) 7-T Fredkin] -> g, a: 0 -> c1 = f&~g [(0 2) Fredkin], Bell decoders (0,1),(2,3), w01 toggled onto p_r inside the H(f) window): the a line is not uncomputed but converted, a: c1 -> p_r&~g by one rccx that reads the raw s_r wire ((f^p_r)&~g cancels the f part of c1, so f is not read; cx(f -> p_r) moved after it), then a fused second toggle with p_r&p_l gives a = h = [p = 3] = p_r p_t ~p_l; with h on a line k0 = [p=3] = (chi_rtl - chi_rtlh)/2 needs 2 Walsh terms instead of 4, so the R_x support is 7 terms (rtl, rtlh, rtlW, rtvW, tlV, rtlV, rtlWV; 6 x 2 beta, 1 x 4 beta; parent per-class k pi/2 shifts reused, no new angle tuning) walked in 9 CX from the free start {t, g} to the free end {r, t, l}, with w23 toggled onto a inside the window (a: h <-> h^w23, self-inverse word); 89 CX (+6: one extra AND pair), T_eps 514 (-124), depth_CT 1246 (-275), 10 qubits.
